correctness.rationale: Exact original N×N Gabor matrix Fourier orthogonality yields p disjoint 2×2 Gram operator blocks with correct wrap-around swap. The rate-four complex Wishart survival law is exact. For adjacent indicators a conditional Gaussian decomposition gives O(epsilon^2(1+|log epsilon|)) joint small-eigenvalue bound; other blocks are independent beyond cyclic nearest neighbors. The standard dependency-graph Chen–Stein inequality gives total variation O_t(log p/p) at epsilon=t/p and the independent nonadjacent subfamily bounds the tails sufficiently to justify all r>0 moments. Direct saved-package full-matrix and statistical checks were run, but numerical simulations are not the infinity proof.

originality.rationale: Inspected the closest subgroup finite-Gabor structural theorem (arXiv:2605.16139, Theorem 1.1 and Section 5), two random finite-Gabor studies (arXiv:1902.01062 Section 2-3 and arXiv:2509.01325 Section 4-6), and relevant Wishart/Poisson theory. None of the inspected claims yields the sharp rate-four minimum law with the dependent cyclic block count and positive-moment convergence. A known log-volume theorem on the exact same model is distinct and insufficient for the minimum. Residual risk remains for independently indexed overlapping-Gram extreme-value results.

value.rationale: The least eigenvalue of a square random Gabor frame operator is the exact lower frame constant controlling inverse stability and worst-case noise amplification. A sharp dimension-scaled rate-four law, quantitative Poisson count despite overlapping Gaussian fibers, and convergence of all positive moments address reconstruction stability not characterized by block-existence or log-volume literature. Its specialized Gaussian geometry and absence of universality claims are acknowledged.
